newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Sierra Leone rebel chief incommunicado in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel chief incommunicado in Nigeria.

text.p: Nigerian authorities on Friday cut off communication to Sierra Leonean rebel leader Foday Sankoh who has declared his support for an army coup at home that West Africa is trying to reverse, officials said.
"You can no longer reach him," one official said.
Sankoh has been kept in a luxury hotel in the Nigerian capital Abuja for the past two months.
He arrived in Lagos in March, saying he wanted to see military ruler General Sani Abacha but has so far met no senior Nigerian official.

Until Wednesday when he ordered members of his Revolutionary United Front (RUF) to join the low-ranking officers who seized power in Freetown on Sunday, Sankoh could be reached by telephone at his $500 a night Abuja Sheraton and Towers Hotel suite.
"There is a 'do not disturb sign' on his telephone and we can't reach him," said a telephone attendant at the hotel.

Sankoh heads the RUF which fought Sierra Leone troops in a civil war that began in 1991. He reached an agreement with the deposed democratically elected government of Sierra Leone last November to end the war that killed 10,000 people, but skirmishes persisted.
Sankoh said earliert this week that he had accepted an invitation from the coup leaders to join them because he wanted security and peace restored to his country.

Military-ruled Nigeria has so far made no public comment on the events in Sierra Leone, where it has massed troops with other West African countries and is expected to try to restore the deposed government.
